sub: Five moves that help a plant recruit workers and win buyers with the same marketing.

slides.title: Treat your careers page like a sales page
slides.body:
Show the shifts, the pay range if you can share it, and real photos of the floor and the team.
Make applying take two minutes on a phone.
slides.tip: Ask a recent hire what almost stopped them from applying.

slides.title: Your Google profile recruits too
slides.body:
Job seekers and buyers both search your name on Google first.
Add photos of the plant and products, keep hours current, and post your openings as updates.
slides.tip: Add 5 new photos a month. Fresh profiles look like busy companies.

slides.title: Pick the right channel for each audience
slides.body:
LinkedIn reaches buyers, engineers and supervisors.
Facebook reaches the hometown workforce and their families, who often tell them about the job.
slides.tip: Same story, two versions: one for buyers, one for workers.

slides.title: Show the work in 20 seconds
slides.body:
A short clip of a machine running, a part coming off the line or a team finishing a big order does double duty.
Buyers see capability. Job seekers see where they would work.
slides.tip: Film vertical, no music needed, one clear caption.

slides.title: Track what brings applicants and quotes
slides.body:
Use one form for job applications and one for quote requests, and record where each came from in your CRM.
Then put next month's effort where the results came from.
slides.tip: Ask every new hire and new customer: how did you hear about us?
